what: What did each Lunenburg town employee earn in 1968?
why: `report-gross-wages` holds per-employee earnings from the 1995-2010 reports and FY2011-FY2025. The 1968 annual town report prints no wage list: the full text was searched for wages, gross, payroll and salary and found only aggregates (the accountant's wage lines in the schedule, p34-46; the Treasurer's payroll deductions, p27-28 and p33), the Personnel Board's essay (p12) and the proposed salary schedule (p13), and the School Personnel listing (p120-131), which names staff, subject, years and year appointed and prints no pay (sources/data/report-tables/1968/). — closes: the Town's calendar-1968 payroll register (W-2 totals by employee) from the Treasurer's office.

what: What were the town's non-union salary grades and step rates actually in force in 1968?
why: `salary-schedule` and `report-classification-plan` read Schedule A from the 2010 report and FY2011 onward. The 1968 report prints the Personnel Board's PROPOSED schedule for the March 1, 1969 meeting (p13, landed as `report-proposed-salary-schedule`) and, in the warrant, the vote of March 4, 1968 substituting the schedule dated March 2, 1968 (text p74), but not that schedule itself; searched classification, salary schedule, grade and step. — closes: the Personnel Board's Classification and Salary Schedule dated March 2, 1968, and the March 1, 1969 vote on the proposal.

what: What did each special revenue fund take in, spend and carry forward in 1968, town-wide?
why: `special-revenue-funds` holds forward, receipts, disbursements and balance by fund from the 1995-2010 reports. The 1968 report prints the revolving funds' YEAR-END balances only, as lines of the balance sheet (p22 `Revolving Funds`: School Lunch 1,622.50, School Athletics 438.31), the school lunch and athletic accounts inside the School Department's own reports (p136, p142), and revenue lines in the Treasurer's receipts (p27-29); no town-wide receipts-and-disbursements schedule by fund. Searched special revenue and revolving: the only hit is p22 (sources/data/report-tables/1968/). — closes: the Town Accountant's calendar-1968 special revenue fund ledger.

what: What was appropriated, spent and carried forward on each capital project fund in 1968?
why: `report-capital-projects` holds a separate capital project fund schedule from the 2001-2010 reports. The 1968 report prints no such schedule: the accountant's schedule lists each special article with its balance (p34-46), the balance sheet carries the unexpended appropriation balances (p23, including Middle School 354,997.01) and no capital plan is printed; so whether any project sat in a separate fund is not shown. Searched capital project and capital plan: no hit (the only `capital` hits are a school budget line and a vote on capital punishment) (sources/data/report-tables/1968/). — closes: the Town Accountant's calendar-1968 capital projects fund ledger.

what: What was Lunenburg's assessed valuation by property class, its levy, overlay and new growth for 1968?
why: `report-valuation` holds the valuation and levy history from the 1987-2010 reports. The 1968 report prints the assessed valuation as lines of the opening facts page (p5: $11,701,850 real estate, $1,105,460 personal property, tax rate $115.50), the net amount raised by taxation at four dates (p11, landed), and the Assessors' prose on the tax rate (p11); no recapitulation of the levy, the overlay or growth. The overlay appears only as a reserve, a deficit and a funding source (p22-23, p46, p70-71). The tax rate of $115.50 on a $11.7 million valuation is as printed; this extract does not establish what proportion of full value the assessments were. Searched valuation, overlay, tax rate, levy and growth (sources/data/report-tables/1968/). — closes: the Assessors' 1968 tax rate recapitulation (the Tax Recap sheet filed with the State).

what: How many weighing and measuring devices did the Sealer test in 1968, and what did sealing bring in by device?
why: `report-weights-measures` holds the Sealer's device counts and `sealing-fee-schedule` the fee per device from the 2001-2010 reports. The 1968 report gives the year's totals in prose on p50 (114 weighing devices inspected, 111 found correct and sealed, one pump and two scales condemned) and the Treasurer's receipts one line, `Inspector of Weights and Measures` (p28), with no count or fee by device type. Searched weights and measures, sealer, sealing (sources/data/report-tables/1968/). — closes: the Inspector of Weights and Measures' 1968 test and fee record.
